cases.evidence_note: p970 p. 16, Example 5, entire scholarship included: "The qualified education expenses would be $6,000, and the AGI and MAGI would be $29,625. The tax liability before any credits would be $603. Jane would be able to receive a $1,603 American opportunity credit ($1,000 refundable and $603 nonrefundable), a $1,700 additional child tax credit, and a $3,325 EIC. In total, Jane would be able to receive a tax refund of $6,025." Class A covers lines 11b, 16, 8, 19, 29, 28, 27a and 33/34; line 27 is the $4,000 cap of the stated $6,000 and line 7 $2,500 follows. Schedule 1 line 8r $5,500, worksheet line 2a $0. The EIC at $3,325 requires the line 8r scholarship to be outside earned income (AGI phase-out). Jane is 28, unmarried, files head of household with her 10-year-old qualifying child (EIC and child tax credit), first-year full-time certificate student; wages $24,125 on a W-2 with no withholding and no other income or adjustments, except the scholarship she includes in income, entered on Schedule 1 line 8r. "Jane and the college meet all the requirements" is read as Form 1098-T and EIN available, line 23 No, line 24 Yes, line 25 No, line 26 No; born before 2002, so the line 7 refundability test does not apply.
